---
title: "08 Stability of the factor structure across the exploratory and validation samples"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    theme: readable
params:
  # Exploratory sample (phase 2.2): -3 ... +3, rare options collapsed (<= 2.5%)
  exploratory_file: "phase2-2-item-reduction/data/prepared/ratings-stimulus_collapsed.csv"
  # Validation sample (phase 3, step 00): 1 ... 7, rare options collapsed (<= 2.5%)
  validation_file: "phase3-validation/00_collapse-categories/output/multigroup_ratings.csv"
  # Criteria for a meaningful loss of fit between invariance levels (Chen, 2007)
  delta_cfi: 0.010
  delta_rmsea: 0.015
  # Flag a standardized loading that changes at least this much between samples
  delta_loading: 0.10
---

This notebook tests whether the claim "the Visualization component is the unstable part"
holds, with three analyses:

1. **Measurement invariance across samples.** Multi-group CFA with the **sample** as the
   group (exploratory vs. validation): configural, metric (equal loadings) and scalar
   (equal loadings and intercepts). When metric or scalar invariance fails, the constraints
   that contribute most to the misfit are freed one at a time (partial invariance), to see
   which items differ between the samples.
2. **Standardized loadings side by side.** The same CFA in each sample separately, item by
   item, with the difference.
3. **The same EFA in both samples.** EFA of the 13 items with the specification of step 06
   (smoothed polychoric correlations, MinRes, Promax, 3 and 4 factors), compared with Tucker's
   congruence coefficients and each item's primary factor.

The claim is supported if the items that are not invariant, the loadings that change and the
items that move between factors are mainly the **visualization** items (and, with them, the
cognitive-value items they mix with in `4_Factor_C`), while the **intuitiveness** items stay put.

Specification of the CFAs: ML (lavaan default), `missing = "fiml"`, collapsed data, as in
steps 05–07. Structures tested: `3_Factor_A` (the final model) and `4_Factor_C` (from the EFA
of the validation sample).

Points to keep in mind:

* The exploratory scale (−3 … +3) is **recoded to 1 … 7** (+4), so intercepts are comparable
  in the scalar model. This does not change loadings, fit or correlations.
* Rare options were collapsed **within each sample** with the same rule (≤ 2.5%). An option can
  therefore be merged in one sample and not in the other, which can shift an intercept a little.
* The tools differ between samples (Gephi, Power BI, Qlik, Tableau, JMP vs. Tableau, JMP, Excel,
  Data Studio, Power BI), and so do the populations. Non-invariance across samples mixes all
  these differences; it does not say which one causes it.
* The items of `3_Factor_A` were selected on the exploratory sample, and `4_Factor_C` was derived
  from the validation sample.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lavaan)
library(psych)
library(polycor)
library(knitr)
library(openxlsx)

# psych may use several cores on macOS/Linux; one core keeps results reproducible (as in step 06)
options(mc.cores = 1)

phase_dir  <- here("phase3-validation")
output_dir <- file.path(phase_dir, "08_cross-sample-stability", "output")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 1. Data

```{r data}
codebook <- read.csv(file.path(phase_dir, "data", "codebook", "items.csv"))
items    <- codebook$short_name

# Exploratory: item codes -> short names, scale -3..+3 -> 1..7
expl_path <- here(params$exploratory_file); stopifnot(file.exists(expl_path))
expl_raw  <- read.csv(expl_path, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
stopifnot(all(codebook$code %in% names(expl_raw)))
expl <- expl_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(stimulus) & stimulus != "") %>%
  select(stimulus, all_of(codebook$code))
names(expl)[match(codebook$code, names(expl))] <- items
expl[items] <- expl[items] + 4
expl$sample <- "exploratory"

# Validation
val_path <- here(params$validation_file); stopifnot(file.exists(val_path))
val <- read.csv(val_path, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") %>%
  select(stimulus, all_of(items))
val$sample <- "validation"

both <- bind_rows(expl, val)
both$sample <- factor(both$sample, levels = c("exploratory", "validation"))

stopifnot(all(range(unlist(expl[items]), na.rm = TRUE) %in% 1:7),
          all(range(unlist(val[items]),  na.rm = TRUE) %in% 1:7))
kable(both %>% count(sample, stimulus), caption = "Participants per sample and tool")

# Answer options left after collapsing, per item and sample
options_left <- both %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(items), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(item, sample) %>%
  summarise(options = paste(sort(unique(value)), collapse = " "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = options) %>%
  mutate(same = exploratory == validation)
kable(options_left, caption = "Answer options left after collapsing (1 ... 7)")

writeLines(c(paste("exploratory_file:", expl_path), paste("md5:", tools::md5sum(expl_path)),
             paste("validation_file:", val_path),   paste("md5:", tools::md5sum(val_path)),
             paste("run at:", Sys.time())),
           file.path(output_dir, "run_info.txt"))
```

## 2. Structures

Copied from step 06.

```{r structures}
structures <- list(
  "3_Factor_A" = list(
    visualization   = c('VisFaithful', 'VisSimpleUnderstand', 'VisAppropriate', 'VisSysRetrieveInfo', 'VisRemember', 'VisTrialError'),
    cognitive_value = c('CogSysThinkDeep', 'CogSysUseful', 'CogSysEnjoy', 'CogTaskComplete'),
    intuitiveness   = c('IntSysSimpleUnderstand', 'IntSysEasyStart', 'IntAnalysisConfigure')
  ),
  "4_Factor_C" = list(
    visual_interaction = c('VisSimpleUnderstand', 'VisRemember', 'VisTrialError', 'VisSysRetrieveInfo'),
    effectiveness      = c('CogSysUseful', 'VisFaithful', 'VisAppropriate', 'CogTaskComplete'),
    cognitive_value    = c('CogSysThinkDeep', 'CogSysEnjoy'),
    intuitiveness      = c('IntSysSimpleUnderstand', 'IntSysEasyStart', 'IntAnalysisConfigure')
  )
)
build_syntax <- function(f) paste(sapply(names(f), function(n)
  paste0(n, " =~ ", paste(f[[n]], collapse = " + "))), collapse = "\n")

# Content block of each item in the codebook (Visualization / Cognitive value / Intuitiveness)
item_block <- setNames(codebook$factor, codebook$short_name)
```

## 3. Functions

```{r functions}
fit_cfa <- function(syntax, data, group = NULL, group.equal = "", group.partial = "") {
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers(
    cfa(syntax, data = data, group = group, missing = "fiml",
        group.equal = group.equal, group.partial = group.partial),
    warning = function(w) { warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(fit)) attr(fit, "warnings") <- unique(warns)
  fit
}

fit_row <- function(fit, structure, level, freed = "") {
  fm <- fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "bic"))
  fm <- setNames(round(as.numeric(fm), 4), names(fm))
  data.frame(structure = structure, level = level, freed = freed, as.list(fm),
             admissible = suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check")),
             warnings = gsub("\\s+", " ", paste(attr(fit, "warnings"), collapse = " | ")),
             row.names = NULL)
}

# Equality constraints of a fitted model, labelled as lavaan's group.partial expects
# ("factor=~item" for loadings, "item~1" for intercepts), with the univariate score test
score_tests <- function(fit) {
  pt <- parTable(fit)
  st <- lavTestScore(fit)$uni
  lab <- function(p) {
    r <- pt[pt$plabel == p & pt$group == 1, ]
    if (r$op == "=~") paste0(r$lhs, "=~", r$rhs) else paste0(r$lhs, r$op, r$rhs)
  }
  st$parameter <- vapply(st$lhs, lab, "")
  st[order(-st$X2), c("parameter", "X2", "df", "p.value")]
}

# Free, one at a time, the constraint with the largest score test until the loss of fit
# against the reference model is within the delta criteria (or nothing significant is left).
# type = "loadings" frees loadings ("f=~item"); type = "intercepts" frees intercepts ("item~1"),
# keeping the loadings already freed in the metric step (start_freed).
param_item <- function(p) sub("~1$", "", sub(".*=~", "", p))

partial_invariance <- function(syntax, structure, level, group.equal, ref_fit, type,
                               start_freed = character(0), max_steps = 10) {
  freed <- start_freed; rows <- list(); steps <- list()
  ref <- fitMeasures(ref_fit, c("cfi", "rmsea"))
  pattern <- if (type == "loadings") "=~" else "~1$"
  fit <- NULL
  for (k in 0:max_steps) {
    fit <- fit_cfa(syntax, both, group = "sample", group.equal = group.equal,
                   group.partial = if (length(freed)) freed else "")
    if (is.null(fit)) break
    fm <- fitMeasures(fit, c("cfi", "rmsea"))
    d_cfi <- unname(ref["cfi"] - fm["cfi"]); d_rmsea <- unname(fm["rmsea"] - ref["rmsea"])
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- cbind(
      fit_row(fit, structure, level, paste(setdiff(freed, start_freed), collapse = "; ")),
      delta_cfi = round(d_cfi, 4), delta_rmsea = round(d_rmsea, 4))
    if (d_cfi <= params$delta_cfi && d_rmsea <= params$delta_rmsea) break
    st <- score_tests(fit)
    st <- st[grepl(pattern, st$parameter) & !st$parameter %in% freed & st$p.value < .05, ]
    if (nrow(st) == 0) break
    steps[[length(steps) + 1]] <- data.frame(structure = structure, level = level, step = k + 1,
                                             st[1, ], block = unname(item_block[param_item(st$parameter[1])]),
                                             row.names = NULL)
    freed <- c(freed, st$parameter[1])
  }
  list(fit = fit, freed = freed, rows = bind_rows(rows), steps = bind_rows(steps))
}
```

## 4. Test 1: measurement invariance across samples

Each level is compared with the one before it. A level holds when CFI drops by at most
`r params$delta_cfi` and RMSEA rises by at most `r params$delta_rmsea`. The likelihood-ratio
test is shown as well; with N ≈ 1,000 it rejects small differences.

```{r invariance}
inv_rows <- list(); lrt_rows <- list(); partial_rows <- list(); freed_steps <- list()

for (s in names(structures)) {
  syn <- build_syntax(structures[[s]])
  configural <- fit_cfa(syn, both, group = "sample")
  metric     <- fit_cfa(syn, both, group = "sample", group.equal = "loadings")
  scalar     <- fit_cfa(syn, both, group = "sample", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

  tab <- bind_rows(fit_row(configural, s, "configural"),
                   fit_row(metric, s, "metric"),
                   fit_row(scalar, s, "scalar")) %>%
    mutate(delta_cfi = round(lag(cfi) - cfi, 4), delta_rmsea = round(rmsea - lag(rmsea), 4),
           holds = ifelse(is.na(delta_cfi), NA,
                          delta_cfi <= params$delta_cfi & delta_rmsea <= params$delta_rmsea))
  inv_rows[[s]] <- tab

  lrt <- as.data.frame(lavTestLRT(configural, metric, scalar))
  lrt_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(structure = s, level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar"),
                              round(lrt, 4), row.names = NULL)

  # Partial invariance: metric against configural; then scalar against the (partial) metric model
  pm <- partial_invariance(syn, s, "metric", "loadings", configural, type = "loadings")
  ps <- partial_invariance(syn, s, "scalar", c("loadings", "intercepts"), pm$fit,
                           type = "intercepts", start_freed = pm$freed)
  partial_rows[[s]] <- bind_rows(pm$rows, ps$rows)
  freed_steps[[s]]  <- bind_rows(pm$steps, ps$steps)
}

inv_tab     <- bind_rows(inv_rows)
lrt_tab     <- bind_rows(lrt_rows)
partial_tab <- bind_rows(partial_rows)
freed_tab   <- bind_rows(freed_steps)
rownames(freed_tab) <- NULL

show <- c("structure", "level", "chisq", "df", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "delta_cfi", "delta_rmsea", "holds", "admissible")
kable(inv_tab[, show], digits = 3, caption = "Invariance across samples (group = sample)")
kable(lrt_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Likelihood-ratio tests")
kable(partial_tab[, c("structure", "level", "freed", "cfi", "rmsea", "delta_cfi", "delta_rmsea", "admissible")],
      digits = 3, caption = "Partial invariance: constraints freed one at a time")
kable(freed_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Constraints freed, in order, with the content block of the item")
```

## 5. Test 2: standardized loadings in each sample

```{r loadings}
load_rows <- list()
for (s in names(structures)) {
  syn <- build_syntax(structures[[s]])
  for (smp in levels(both$sample)) {
    fit <- fit_cfa(syn, filter(both, sample == smp))
    load_rows[[paste(s, smp)]] <- standardizedSolution(fit) %>%
      filter(op == "=~") %>%
      transmute(structure = s, sample = smp, factor = lhs, item = rhs,
                lambda = est.std, ci_lower = ci.lower, ci_upper = ci.upper)
  }
}
loadings_long <- bind_rows(load_rows)

loadings_wide <- loadings_long %>%
  select(structure, factor, item, sample, lambda) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = lambda) %>%
  mutate(block = item_block[item],
         change = validation - exploratory,
         flagged = abs(change) >= params$delta_loading) %>%
  arrange(structure, factor, item)

kable(loadings_wide, digits = 3, caption = "Standardized loadings by sample (change = validation - exploratory)")

kable(loadings_wide %>% group_by(structure, block) %>%
        summarise(items = n(), mean_abs_change = mean(abs(change)), max_abs_change = max(abs(change)),
                  flagged = sum(flagged), .groups = "drop"),
      digits = 3, caption = "Change in loadings by content block")
```

## 6. Test 3: the same EFA in both samples

Same specification as step 06: smoothed polychoric correlations (`polycor::hetcor`), MinRes,
Promax, all tools pooled. Factors of the two samples are matched by Tucker's congruence
coefficient (φ). Common reading: φ ≥ 0.95 equal, 0.85–0.94 fairly similar, < 0.85 different.

```{r efa}
make_corrM <- function(d) {
  d <- as.data.frame(lapply(d, ordered), check.names = FALSE)
  cm <- polycor::hetcor(d, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", std.err = FALSE, ML = FALSE)$correlations
  dimnames(cm) <- list(names(d), names(d))
  if (any(eigen(cm)$values <= 0)) cm <- psych::cor.smooth(cm)
  cm
}

efa_one <- function(d, nf) {
  fa_fit <- psych::fa(make_corrM(d), nfactors = nf, n.obs = nrow(d), rotate = "promax", fm = "minres")
  L <- unclass(fa_fit$loadings)
  colnames(L) <- paste0("F", seq_len(nf))
  L
}

efa_rows <- list(); congruence_rows <- list(); primary_rows <- list()
for (nf in 3:4) {
  Le <- efa_one(expl[items], nf)
  Lv <- efa_one(val[items], nf)

  # Match each validation factor to an exploratory one (greedy, by |phi|)
  phi <- psych::factor.congruence(Le, Lv)
  match_v <- rep(NA_integer_, nf); used <- integer(0)
  for (k in order(-apply(abs(phi), 2, max))) {
    cand <- setdiff(seq_len(nf), used)
    best <- cand[which.max(abs(phi[cand, k]))]
    match_v[k] <- best; used <- c(used, best)
  }
  # Re-label validation factors with the exploratory label they match (and flip signs if needed)
  Lv_m <- Lv
  for (k in seq_len(nf)) Lv_m[, k] <- Lv[, k] * sign(phi[match_v[k], k])
  colnames(Lv_m) <- colnames(Le)[match_v]
  Lv_m <- Lv_m[, colnames(Le), drop = FALSE]

  congruence_rows[[nf]] <- data.frame(
    n_factors = nf, exploratory_factor = colnames(Le),
    validation_factor = colnames(Lv)[match(colnames(Le), colnames(Le)[match_v])],
    phi = round(diag(psych::factor.congruence(Le, Lv_m)), 3))

  prim <- function(L) colnames(L)[apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)]
  primary_rows[[nf]] <- data.frame(
    n_factors = nf, item = items, block = item_block[items],
    primary_exploratory = prim(Le), loading_exploratory = round(apply(Le, 1, function(x) x[which.max(abs(x))]), 3),
    primary_validation = prim(Lv_m), loading_validation = round(apply(Lv_m, 1, function(x) x[which.max(abs(x))]), 3),
    row.names = NULL) %>%
    mutate(same_factor = primary_exploratory == primary_validation)

  efa_rows[[nf]] <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(n_factors = nf, sample = "exploratory", item = items, round(Le, 3), row.names = NULL),
    data.frame(n_factors = nf, sample = "validation (matched)", item = items, round(Lv_m, 3), row.names = NULL))
}
congruence_tab <- bind_rows(congruence_rows)
primary_tab    <- bind_rows(primary_rows)
efa_tab        <- bind_rows(efa_rows)

kable(congruence_tab, caption = "Tucker's congruence between the samples' factors")
kable(primary_tab, caption = "Primary factor of each item (validation factors relabelled to match the exploratory ones)")
kable(primary_tab %>% group_by(n_factors, block) %>%
        summarise(items = n(), moved = sum(!same_factor), .groups = "drop"),
      caption = "Items that change primary factor, by content block")
```

## 7. Follow-up A: item distributions in each sample

Hypothesis from the first run (2026-11-05): the fourth factor of `4_Factor_C` (effectiveness:
CogSysUseful, CogTaskComplete, VisAppropriate, VisFaithful) appears only in the validation
sample because these items have the strongest ceiling there, and items with similarly skewed
distributions can group together for that reason alone (a "difficulty factor"). If so, these
four items should be the ones whose distributions are most piled up at the top of the scale in
validation, and whose distributions change most between samples.

Computed on the collapsed data, on the 1 … 7 scale.

```{r distributions}
dist_tab <- both %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(items), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(item, sample) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value),
            skew = psych::skew(value), kurtosis = psych::kurtosi(value),
            pct_7 = mean(value == 7), pct_6_7 = mean(value >= 6),
            n_options = n_distinct(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(block = item_block[item],
         effectiveness_item = item %in% structures[["4_Factor_C"]]$effectiveness)

dist_wide <- dist_tab %>%
  select(item, block, effectiveness_item, sample, mean, skew, pct_6_7, n_options) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = c(mean, skew, pct_6_7, n_options)) %>%
  mutate(mean_change = mean_validation - mean_exploratory,
         skew_change = skew_validation - skew_exploratory,
         pct_6_7_change = pct_6_7_validation - pct_6_7_exploratory) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_6_7_validation))

kable(dist_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Item distributions by sample (collapsed data, 1 ... 7)")
kable(dist_wide, digits = 3, caption = "Distributions side by side, sorted by % of answers 6-7 in validation")

kable(dist_wide %>% group_by(effectiveness_item) %>%
        summarise(items = n(),
                  pct_6_7_expl = mean(pct_6_7_exploratory), pct_6_7_valid = mean(pct_6_7_validation),
                  skew_expl = mean(skew_exploratory), skew_valid = mean(skew_validation),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      digits = 3, caption = "Effectiveness items of 4_Factor_C vs. the other nine items (means)")

# Rank of the four effectiveness items among the 13 by % of answers 6-7 in validation (1 = most)
kable(dist_wide %>% mutate(rank_pct_6_7_validation = rank(-pct_6_7_validation)) %>%
        filter(effectiveness_item) %>% select(item, pct_6_7_validation, rank_pct_6_7_validation),
      digits = 3, caption = "Where the effectiveness items rank in ceiling (validation)")
```

## 8. Follow-up B: where the misfit of 3_Factor_A comes from

Test 1 shows that loadings and intercepts of `3_Factor_A` are equivalent across samples, yet
the pooled fit is much worse in validation (CFI 0.971 vs. 0.900, step 07). The misfit must then
come from parts of the model the invariance tests do not constrain, such as residual
covariances (local dependence) or cross-loadings. Modification indices (MI) of the CFA in each
sample show which ones. `sepc.all` is the standardized expected change: the residual correlation
or cross-loading the model would estimate if that parameter were freed.

```{r modification indices}
mi_rows <- list()
syn_3a <- build_syntax(structures[["3_Factor_A"]])
for (smp in levels(both$sample)) {
  fit <- fit_cfa(syn_3a, filter(both, sample == smp))
  mi <- modindices(fit, sort. = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
  mi <- mi[mi$op %in% c("~~", "=~") & !(mi$op == "~~" & mi$lhs == mi$rhs), ]
  mi_rows[[smp]] <- mi %>%
    transmute(sample = smp,
              parameter = paste(lhs, op, rhs),
              type = ifelse(op == "~~", "residual covariance", "cross-loading"),
              block_lhs = ifelse(op == "~~", item_block[lhs], lhs),
              block_rhs = item_block[rhs],
              mi = round(mi, 2), sepc.all = round(sepc.all, 3))
}
mi_tab <- bind_rows(mi_rows)

for (smp in levels(both$sample))
  print(kable(head(filter(mi_tab, sample == smp), 15),
              caption = paste("Top 15 modification indices,", smp, "sample")))

# Total MI by pair of content blocks (where the local misfit concentrates)
kable(mi_tab %>%
        mutate(pair = ifelse(type == "residual covariance",
                             paste(pmin(block_lhs, block_rhs), "-", pmax(block_lhs, block_rhs)),
                             paste("cross-loading on", block_lhs, "of", block_rhs, "item"))) %>%
        group_by(sample, pair) %>%
        summarise(n = n(), total_mi = sum(mi), max_mi = max(mi), .groups = "drop") %>%
        arrange(sample, desc(total_mi)),
      digits = 1, caption = "Modification indices summed by pair of content blocks")
```
